root_cause.text: In drm/i915 NV12 plane handling, unlink_nv12_plane() was invoked after plane_atomic_check() and could clear fields in intel_plane_state for a plane transitioning from linked Y-plane use to normal use, causing state corruption due to incorrect operation ordering.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states “unlink_nv12_plane() will clobber parts of the plane state potentially already set up by plane_atomic_check(), so we must make sure not to call the two in the wrong order,” and the patch moves unlinking earlier by calling unlink_nv12_plane() in intel_plane_set_invisible() before state setup and adding an early return when planar_linked_plane is NULL.

intent_record.intent_summary: Unlink NV12 plane state when hiding a plane to avoid leaving stale NV12 associations after the plane is marked invisible.
intent_record.what: A forward declaration for static function unlink_nv12_plane(struct intel_crtc_state *crtc_state, struct intel_plane_state *plane_state) was added, and intel_plane_set_invisible() was modified to call unlink_nv12_plane(crtc_state, plane_state) before clearing the plane's bits from active_planes, scaled_planes, and nv12_planes.
intent_record.how: When a plane is made invisible, the code now explicitly removes any NV12 plane linkage associated with that plane before updating the CRTC plane bitmasks, preventing stale NV12 association state from remaining after the plane is disabled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null check in unlink_nv12_plane() to avoid unlinking when no planar linked plane is present.
intent_record.what: A new early-return guard was added at the start of unlink_nv12_plane() to check whether plane_state->planar_linked_plane is NULL, and if so, exit the function before clearing the link and continuing with the existing unlink logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now skips unlink processing when no linked plane exists, preventing unnecessary state changes or invalid unlink operations on an already unlinked or never-linked plane state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always unlink matching NV12 planes during validation to clear stale plane linkage state.
intent_record.what: The conditional check guarding unlink_nv12_plane(crtc_state, plane_state) was removed, so the function is now called unconditionally for each plane on the matching pipe instead of only when plane_state->planar_linked_plane is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, every relevant plane is forcibly unlinked from NV12 plane linkage during this check pass, ensuring stale or inconsistent linkage state is cleared even when planar_linked_plane is not set, rather than skipping unlinking based on that field.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it directly shows the ordering of NV12 plane unlink/link handling within the function. The root cause says unlink_nv12_plane() was invoked after plane_atomic_check(), which could clear intel_plane_state fields for a plane transitioning from linked Y-plane use to normal use. This function explicitly performs unlinking of any previously linked plane state at lines 1301-1311: "Destroy all old plane links" and `if (plane_state->planar_linked_plane) unlink_nv12_plane(crtc_state, plane_state);`. It then later rebuilds links only if `crtc_state->nv12_planes` is set (lines 1313-1349). The vulnerable construct is the unconditional clearing of prior planar links in the plane state via `unlink_nv12_plane()` for planes in the new state. For a plane transitioning away from NV12 linked usage, this can clear fields in `intel_plane_state` after prior validation/checking has already occurred, matching the described corruption due to incorrect operation ordering. There is no indication in this function of the fix that would move this unlinking before plane_atomic_check() or otherwise preserve state correctly; instead, the function still contains the unlink logic in the problematic form.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it directly shows the ordering of NV12 unlink/relink operations. The vulnerable construct is present in the first loop: `if (plane_state->planar_linked_plane) unlink_nv12_plane(crtc_state, plane_state);` at lines 1305-1311. Per the root cause, calling `unlink_nv12_plane()` after `plane_atomic_check()` can clear fields in `intel_plane_state` for a plane transitioning from linked Y-plane use to normal use, causing state corruption. This function performs unconditional unlinking of all previously linked planes before rebuilding links, and there is no indication here of the fix that would avoid corrupting state by changing the ordering relative to plane checks or otherwise preserving the state. The later relinking logic (`link_nv12_planes(...)` at line 1348) does not address the ordering bug; it only reconstructs links for planes in `crtc_state->nv12_planes`. Thus the vulnerable logic is present and the fix is not yet in this function.
